app.name: Enbywiki
app.tagline: An open, bilingual history of transgender communities
app.description: From the temple singers of ancient Sumer to the movements of today — a source-minded timeline of transgender lives, cultures, and resistance within the LGBTQ+ story.

home.title: A History of Transgender Communities
home.subtitle: From the priests of ancient Sumer to the activists of today — a bilingual, source-minded timeline of transgender lives, cultures, and resistance.
home.flagCaption: The Transgender Pride Flag, designed by Monica Helms in 1999.
home.flagAlt: Transgender Pride Flag: light blue, pink, white, pink, light blue stripes
home.timelineSubtitle: Ten chapters moving from antiquity to the present day.
home.referenceSubtitle: People, words, and the place of the "T" within LGBTQ+.
home.whyBody: Transgender people have existed in every recorded era and on every continent, yet their stories are routinely flattened, medicalised, or erased. Enbywiki gathers them into one readable, bilingual timeline — so the long history of gender diversity is available to anyone, in English or 简体中文.
home.noteBody: Historical records use the vocabulary of their time. Where sources use older or now-offensive terms, this wiki explains rather than repeats them uncritically, and it centres the words communities use for themselves.

about.title: About Enbywiki
about.subtitle: A small, independent archive that tries to tell the long history of transgender people clearly, kindly, and in two languages.
about.flagBody: Designed by Monica Helms in 1999, the flag's five stripes carry a deliberate symmetry: whichever way it is flown, it is always correct — a reminder that trans people have always existed and always will.
about.flagBlue: The traditional colour associated with boys.
about.flagPink: The traditional colour associated with girls.
about.flagWhite: People who are transitioning, are intersex, or hold a neutral or undefined gender.
about.missionBody: To collect the history of the "T" within LGBTQ+ into a readable, accessible timeline — from antiquity to the present — and to keep it free and bilingual.
about.methodBody: Entries synthesise mainstream historical and community scholarship. Contested dates are flagged as approximate, and where a claim is debated the text says so rather than smoothing it over.
about.languagesBody: Interface text lives in JSON locale files while the history itself lives in paired English and Simplified Chinese Markdown, so both language versions can grow together.
about.techBody: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, react-markdown, React Router and i18next. The dark mode toggle stores your preference in the browser.
about.licenseBody: This is a non-commercial educational project. The Transgender Pride Flag design is in the public domain. Please share and cite generously.

ancient-world.title: Ancient Origins
ancient-world.description: The earliest recorded lives of gender-diverse people: Sumerian gala priests, Egyptian figures, and the sacred gender roles of the ancient world.

sacred-traditions.title: Sacred & Classical Traditions
sacred-traditions.description: Hijra communities of South Asia, Two-Spirit identities of Indigenous North America, and the gender-variant traditions that colonial powers later criminalised.

medieval-early-modern.title: Medieval to Early Modern
medieval-early-modern.description: Cross-dressing saints, hermaphrodite lore, and the shifting legal and religious treatment of gender variance across Europe and the Islamic world.

colonial-suppression.title: Colonialism & Suppression
colonial-suppression.description: How empire exported binary gender law, criminalised hijra and Two-Spirit life, and pushed trans existence into the shadows.

birth-of-sexology.title: The Birth of Sexology
birth-of-sexology.description: Ulrichs, Hirschfeld and the first scientific language for transgender identity — emancipation or pathologisation?

weimar-institute.title: Weimar & the First Institute
weimar-institute.description: Berlin's Institute for Sexual Science, the first gender clinics, Dora Richter and Lili Elbe — a brief flowering before the Nazis.

midcentury.title: Mid-Century Turbulence
midcentury.description: Nazi book burnings, the postwar clinic boom, Christine Jorgensen, and the work of trans pioneers in the 1950s and 60s.

stonewall-liberation.title: Stonewall & Liberation
stonewall-liberation.description: Compton's Cafeteria, Stonewall, STAR, and the trans women of colour whose leadership shaped the gay liberation movement.

aids-and-90s.title: AIDS, Activism & the 1990s
aids-and-90s.description: The AIDS crisis, Transgender Day of Remembrance, the removal of trans identity from diagnostic disorder lists, and the flag's debut.

twenty-first-century.title: The Twenty-First Century
twenty-first-century.description: Global visibility, legal recognition, gender self-determination laws, and the continuing struggle against backlash.

key-figures.title: Key Figures
key-figures.description: Profiles of the people who shaped transgender history — scholars, activists, artists and martyrs.

glossary.title: Glossary of Terms
glossary.description: Working definitions for transgender, non-binary, gender dysphoria, cisgender and more, in plain language.

transgender-in-lgbtq.title: The 'T' in LGBTQ+
transgender-in-lgbtq.description: How transgender people moved from the margins to the heart of the LGBTQ+ movement — and the tensions that remain.
